name: Edwin Moses
one_line: Lost in August 1977, then won every 400m hurdles race for 9 years, 9 months and 9 days - 122 in a row.

facts.claim: won 122 consecutive races between 1977 and 1987, of which 107 were consecutive finals
facts.note: Wikipedia verbatim: 'Between 1977 and 1987, Moses won 107 consecutive finals (122 consecutive races).' PRECISION MATTERS: 122 races including heats, 107 finals - a script saying only '122 finals' would be wrong.

facts.claim: the streak lasted nine years, nine months, and nine days
facts.note: Wikipedia verbatim: after the 1977 loss he 'did not lose another race for nine years, nine months, and nine days.' The 9-9-9 symmetry is the hook-grade number.

facts.claim: the last man to beat him before the streak was Harald Schmid, in Berlin, 26 August 1977
the streak ended on 4 June 1987 in Madrid, when Danny Harris beat him
after the streak ended, he won his next 10 races in a row
facts.note: THE closer. He answered the only loss in a decade with another streak.

facts.claim: before March 1976 he had run only one 400m hurdles race in his life; that July he was Olympic champion in Montreal
facts.note: The origin beat. Four months from novice to Olympic gold.

facts.claim: studied physics and industrial engineering at Morehouse College, which had no track - he trained at public high school facilities
facts.note: Academic scholarship, not athletic. The world's most dominant athlete trained on borrowed high-school tracks.

facts.claim: set the world record four times; personal best 47.02 in 1983
Olympic gold in 1976 and 1984; could not compete in 1980 (US boycott) despite being mid-streak; bronze in 1988
facts.note: One of his prime Olympics was taken by politics, mid-streak. Congressional Gold Medal as consolation.

comparison.gap_description: 122 straight wins across 9 years, 9 months and 9 days.

story_beat: Before March 1976 he had run exactly one 400m hurdles race; four months later he was Olympic champion. His college had no track, so the man who would dominate the event for a decade trained at public high school facilities while finishing a physics degree.
